title: Galois groups of Keller fibers
W: Find the symmetry group of the preimages of a point under the 2026 Keller maps.
M: Compute the Galois group of the generic fiber of Gallagher's degree-$n$ Keller family for each $n\ge3$.

title: Integer-bijective Keller map
W: Find a polynomial map with Jacobian 1 that shuffles integer points perfectly but has no polynomial inverse.
M: Find $F\in\mathbb{Z}[x]^n$, $\det DF\equiv1$, inducing a bijection of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ but not a polynomial automorphism.

title: Keller maps of degree 4
W: Show that every 3D polynomial map of degree at most 4 with constant Jacobian has a polynomial inverse.
M: Prove $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$, $\deg F\le4$, $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ implies $F$ is an automorphism.

title: Keller maps with integer fibers
W: Show no Jacobian-conjecture counterexample with integer coefficients is injective on integer points but not invertible.
M: Prove every Keller map $F\in\mathbb{Z}[x,y,z]^3$ injective on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ is a polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^3$.

title: Keller monodromy is everything
W: Show every symmetric group appears as the hidden symmetry group of the fibres of some 3D Jacobian-conjecture counterexample.
M: Prove that for each $n\ge3$ there is a non-invertible Keller map $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ of geometric degree $n$ whose generic monodromy group is $S_n$.

title: Minimal degree of a Jacobian counterexample
W: The 2026 counterexamples have degree 7. Find the smallest degree any 3D counterexample can have.
M: Determine $\min\{\deg F: F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ non-invertible Keller map$\}$.

title: Real-rank hyperoperation uniqueness
W: Prove there is exactly one natural way to fill in the operations between addition, multiplication and powers.
M: Prove uniqueness of an analytic family $a[s]b$ on $s\in[1,3]$ under the recursion law plus a log-convexity condition in $s$, and existence.

title: Small Keller maps in 3D
W: The 2026 counterexamples to the Jacobian conjecture have fairly high degree. Is there one of degree 5 or less?
M: Decide whether some $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with $\deg F\le5$ and $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ has no polynomial inverse.

title: Three-pile shuffle group
W: Using the six ways to stack three piles in a perfect shuffle, which rearrangements of the deck can you reach?
M: Determine the subgroup of $S_{3n}$ generated by the six 3-pile perfect shuffles (all pile orders), for every $n$.

title: Blow-up near a wall
W: Show the 2026 forced blow-up mechanism also works in a half-space with no-slip wall, with the singularity on the wall.
M: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ such that Navier–Stokes in $\mathbb{R}^3_+$ with no-slip, from rest, blows up in finite time at a boundary point.

title: Charge on a Fermat conductor
W: Put a unit of electric charge on a perfectly conducting body x⁴+y⁴+z⁴ ≤ 1. Show the surface charge is thinnest at the six flat points and thickest at the eight diagonal points.
M: Let $\mu$ be the Newtonian equilibrium measure of $K=\{x^4+y^4+z^4\le1\}$, with density $\rho$ with respect to surface area on $\partial K$. Prove that $\rho$ attains its minimum exactly at $(\pm1,0,0),(0,\pm1,0),(0,0,\pm1)$ and its maximum exactly at $3^{-1/4}(\pm1,\pm1,\pm1)$.

title: Closed-form Euler blow-up
W: Give smooth starting data for frictionless 3D fluid, written as an explicit formula, that blows up.
M: Find closed-form smooth finite-energy $u_0$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose unforced Euler solution blows up in finite time.

title: Drum tones of superellipses
W: Among regions x^p + y^p ≤ r of unit area, the circle (p = 2) has the lowest tone and the square (p = ∞) is back up high. Show the tone rises steadily as p goes from 2 to infinity.
M: Let $D_p=\{|x|^p+|y|^p\le r_p^p\}$ with $r_p$ chosen so $|D_p|=1$, and let $\lambda_1(p)$ be its first Dirichlet eigenvalue. Prove $\lambda_1$ is strictly increasing on $[2,\infty)$.

title: Fibonacci-modulated growing Jacobi matrix
W: Off-diagonal weights grow like √n but are doubled wherever the Fibonacci word has a 1. Periodic modulations give spectral phase transitions. Decide what this aperiodic one gives.
M: Let $f\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$ be the Fibonacci word and $J$ the Jacobi matrix with $a_n=\sqrt n\,(1+f_n)$, $b_n=0$. Determine the spectral type of $J$; in particular decide whether $J$ has absolutely continuous spectrum.

title: Firebreak with wind
W: How long must a firebreak be to save a round town from a wind-driven fire?
M: For front speed $a+b\cos\theta$ and a disc town at distance $D$, find the minimal length of a curve built at speed $\sigma$ that protects the town.

title: Fluid in a box blows up
W: Show viscous fluid in a closed box with sticky walls can blow up under a smooth push.
M: Construct smooth $f$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes with no-slip in the unit cube blows up in finite time.

title: Hearing tetrahedra
W: Triangles can be heard: their Dirichlet spectrum determines them. Show the same holds for tetrahedra.
M: Prove that two tetrahedra in $\mathbb R^3$ with the same Dirichlet Laplacian spectrum are congruent.

title: Hyperdissipative forced blow-up
W: Fluids with extra strong viscosity never blow up above a known threshold. Show forced blow-up still happens just below it.
M: For $\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u+\nabla p=-(-\Delta)^{\alpha}u+f$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$, construct smooth compactly supported $f$ giving finite-time blow-up from rest for every $\alpha<5/4$.

title: Jacobi matrix of primes
W: Use the primes as the off-diagonal entries of a Jacobi matrix. Known criteria for absolutely continuous spectrum just fail because prime gaps fluctuate. Decide the spectral type.
M: Let $J$ be the Jacobi matrix on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$ with $a_n=p_n$ (the $n$-th prime) and $b_n=0$, which is self-adjoint since $\sum1/p_n=\infty$. Decide whether the spectrum of $J$ is purely absolutely continuous on $\mathbb R$.

title: Kagome Hofstadter butterfly
W: The Harper model on the square lattice has a Cantor spectrum for every irrational flux. Prove the same for electrons hopping on the kagome lattice.
M: Let $H_\alpha$ be the nearest-neighbour magnetic Laplacian on the kagome lattice for a uniform magnetic field with flux $2\pi\alpha$ through each unit cell. Prove that $\sigma(H_\alpha)$ is a Cantor set for every irrational $\alpha$.

title: Multiplicities on the Fermat quartic
W: The surface x⁴+y⁴+z⁴ = 1 has the symmetries of a cube. Show its Laplace eigenvalues never repeat more than symmetry forces, except perhaps finitely often.
M: Let $S=\{x^4+y^4+z^4=1\}$ with the induced metric. Prove that all but finitely many Laplace eigenvalues of $S$ have multiplicity at most $3$.

title: Non-arithmetic tones of the cube
W: Many vibration frequencies of a cube's surface come from the square torus and are rational multiples of π². Show some frequency is not.
M: Let $S$ be the flat unit-cube surface. Prove that some eigenvalue of the Laplacian on $S$ is not a rational multiple of $\pi^2$.

title: Quartic oscillator ground state
W: The lowest energy of the quartic oscillator, −d²/dx² + x⁴, is about 1.0603620905. Show it is irrational.
M: Let $E_0=\min\sigma\big(-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+x^4\big)$ on $L^2(\mathbb R)$. Prove $E_0\notin\mathbb Q$.

title: Smallest force for blow-up
W: How weak can the push be and still make viscous fluid blow up?
M: Find the optimal exponent $a$ with $\inf\{\|f\|_{L^\infty}: \text{NS from rest blows up}\}\asymp \nu^{a}$.

title: Spikes at the primes
W: Put a fixed bump at every prime on the half-line lattice. Prove the electron is localized at energies inside the free band, as it would be if the primes were random.
M: Let $H=\Delta+\lambda\mathbf 1_{\mathbb P}$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$, $\lambda\ne0$. Prove that $H$ has pure point spectrum in $(-2,2)$.

title: Spikes at the squares
W: Put a fixed bump at every perfect square on the half-line lattice. The spectrum has no absolutely continuous part. Prove the states are localized inside the free band.
M: Let $H=\Delta+\lambda\mathbf 1_{\{m^2:m\ge1\}}$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$, $\lambda\ne0$. Prove that the spectral measure of $\delta_1$ restricted to $(-2,2)$ is pure point.

title: Sup norms on the Fermat quartic
W: On a sphere, some eigenfunctions pile up at the poles as much as possible. Show this cannot happen on the surface x⁴+y⁴+z⁴ = 1.
M: Let $S=\{x^4+y^4+z^4=1\}$ with the induced metric and $\Delta\varphi=-\lambda\varphi$, $\|\varphi\|_{L^2(S)}=1$. Prove that $\|\varphi\|_{L^\infty(S)}=o(\lambda^{1/4})$ as $\lambda\to\infty$.

title: Time-independent force
W: Make viscous fluid blow up with a push that never changes in time.
M: Construct smooth compactly supported time-independent $f$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes from rest blows up in finite time.

title: Two-frequency localization
W: Use a potential that is the sum of two cosines with frequencies √2 and √3, and take strong coupling. Prove electrons localize for these specific frequencies, not just for almost every frequency pair.
M: Let $(H_\theta\psi)(n)=\psi(n+1)+\psi(n-1)+10\big(\cos2\pi(n\sqrt2+\theta_1)+\cos2\pi(n\sqrt3+\theta_2)\big)\psi(n)$. Prove that for Lebesgue-a.e. $\theta\in\mathbb T^2$, $H_\theta$ has pure point spectrum with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions.

title: Blank jigsaw
W: A jigsaw with no picture can only be solved from piece shapes. How few edge shapes force a unique solution?
M: Find the asymptotics in $n$ of the least number of edge types such that some $n\times n$ jigsaw has exactly one assembly (up to rotation of the whole).

title: Codes avoiding square distances
W: Find the largest set of binary strings of length n in which no two differ in a perfect-square number of positions. Find the exponential rate.
M: Let $A(n)$ be the largest $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ with $d_H(x,y)$ never a positive perfect square for $x\ne y\in C$. Determine $\lim_n\frac1n\log_2A(n)$.

title: Firefighter on Z³
W: How many firefighters per turn are needed to contain a fire in 3D, as a precise growth rate?
M: Determine $\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)/t$ for the minimal firefighters needed to contain fire on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ by time $t$.

title: Graceful forests with one big tree
W: A forest with c trees and m edges is graceful-forest labelled if its vertices get the labels 0 to m + c − 1 with all edge differences distinct. Show this works whenever there are at least two trees and one of them holds more than half the edges.
M: Prove every forest with $m$ edges and $c\ge2$ components, one of which has more than $m/2$ edges, has a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+c-1\}$ with all $|\ell(u)-\ell(v)|$, $uv\in E$, distinct.

title: Hadwiger's true constant
W: If graphs needing many colors need not contain a full complete-graph minor, find how large a complete minor they must contain.
M: Find $c^*=\liminf_{t}\min\{h(G)/t:\chi(G)\ge t\}$, where $h$ is the Hadwiger number.

title: Monochromatic square-sum triangles, many colours
W: Colour the positive integers with any finite number of colours. Show there are always three numbers of one colour whose pairwise sums are all squares.
M: Prove that for every $r$ and every $r$-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there are distinct $a,b,c$ of one colour with $a+b,a+c,b+c$ all perfect squares.

title: Paley spin glass
W: Spins on F_p interact through Legendre symbols of their differences. The spectral bound caps the ground-state energy at one half times p^{3/2}, and local search gets to about 0.46. Is the bound sharp?
M: For primes $p\equiv1\pmod4$ let $E_p=\max_{\sigma\in\{\pm1\}^{\mathbb F_p}}\sum_{i<j}\left(\frac{j-i}{p}\right)\sigma_i\sigma_j\le\frac12p^{3/2}$. Decide whether $E_p/p^{3/2}\to\frac12$. (Greedy local search from 30 random starts gave ratios $0.461,0.461,0.461,0.456$ for $p=101,197,401,797$.)

title: Petersen Ramsey multiplicity
W: In any two-coloring of a huge complete graph, how many single-color copies of the Petersen graph must appear, at least?
M: Determine the Ramsey multiplicity constant $\lim_n \min_{\text{2-col}} \#\text{mono } P / \#P \text{ in } K_n$ for the Petersen graph $P$.

title: Prime-sum labelling of balanced trees
W: Label a tree with 1 to n so every edge sums to a prime. Parity forces the two sides of the tree to be balanced. Show balance is enough, for large n.
M: Prove every tree on $n\ge n_0$ vertices whose bipartition classes have sizes $\lceil n/2\rceil,\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ admits a bijection $V\to[n]$ with all edge sums prime.

title: Ringel for forests
W: Split a complete graph on 2m + 1 vertices into identical copies of any given forest with m edges.
M: Prove $K_{2m+1}$ decomposes into $2m+1$ copies of any forest with $m$ edges.

title: Small Hadwiger counterexample
W: The claimed counterexamples to Hadwiger's conjecture are astronomically large. Find one under a million vertices.
M: Find $G$ with $|V(G)|<10^6$ and $h(G)<\chi(G)$, or prove every counterexample is larger.

title: Square-sum cliques
W: How many numbers can pairwise add up to perfect squares? Decide if there is a limit.
M: Decide whether $\omega(S_N)$ is bounded, i.e., whether there exist arbitrarily large sets of distinct positive integers with all pairwise sums square.

title: Square-sum coloring
W: Join numbers that add up to a perfect square. Does the number of colors needed stay bounded forever?
M: Decide whether $\sup_N \chi(S_N)<\infty$.

title: Sudoku transversals
W: In every completed big Sudoku, find a set of cells with one in each row, each column and each symbol.
M: Prove every $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku grid, viewed as a Latin square, has a transversal.

title: 3-SAT at density 4
W: Give a fast algorithm that solves almost all random 3-SAT puzzles up to clause density 4.
M: Give a polynomial-time algorithm finding satisfying assignments of random 3-SAT with density $4.0$ with probability $1-o(1)$.

title: Computable connective constants
W: Count the self-avoiding walks of length n on the Cayley graph of a finitely generated group. Their n-th root tends to the connective constant, and upper bounds converge to it. For groups with a solvable word problem, is the connective constant always a computable number?
M: Let $G$ be a finitely generated group with solvable word problem and finite symmetric generating set $S$, let $c_n$ be the number of $n$-step self-avoiding walks from $e$ in the Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(G,S)$, and let $\mu(G,S)=\lim c_n^{1/n}=\inf_n c_n^{1/n}$ (so $\mu$ is upper semicomputable). Is $\mu(G,S)$ a computable real for every such $(G,S)$? If not, give a counterexample. If so, is it computable uniformly from $S$ and an algorithm for the word problem?

title: Finding Huang's vertex
W: Huang's theorem says any set of more than half the corners of an n-dimensional cube contains a corner with at least √n neighbours in the set. When the set is given by a small circuit, how hard is it to find such a corner? Place this search problem among the known classes of total search problems.
M: $\mathrm{HUANG}$: given a Boolean circuit $f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{0,1\}^n$ whose domain is read as $[2^{n-1}+1]$ (inputs beyond $2^{n-1}+1$ are ignored), output either $i\ne j$ with $f(i)=f(j)$, or indices $i,j_1,\dots,j_m$ with $m=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil$ such that $f(j_1),\dots,f(j_m)$ are distinct and each is at Hamming distance 1 from $f(i)$. By Huang's theorem and the pigeonhole principle this is a TFNP problem. Is $\mathrm{HUANG}\in\mathrm{FP}$? Is it in $\mathrm{PPP}$, $\mathrm{PPA}$ or $\mathrm{PLS}$, and is it complete for any standard subclass of TFNP?

title: How much of the real quadratic family is chaotic?
W: For real c between −2 and 1/4, the map x ↦ x² + c has an attracting cycle for an open dense set of c, but the remaining chaotic parameters have positive length. Is the total length of the parameters with an attracting cycle a computable number? It can be approximated from below by listing windows, but no method approximates it from above.
M: Let $H=\{c\in[-2,1/4]: x\mapsto x^2+c\text{ has an attracting periodic orbit}\}$. Is the Lebesgue measure $\lambda(H)$ a computable real? (It is lower semicomputable, and $0<\lambda(H)<9/4$ by Jakobson's theorem.)

title: Information-tight sorting of pattern classes
W: Suppose an array is promised to avoid some fixed pattern (for example, no four entries in the relative order 1, 3, 2, 4). Counting the allowed orders gives a lower bound on the number of comparisons needed to sort it, and Fredman's theorem says this bound plus 2n comparisons always suffice. Is the counting bound always tight up to a negligible error, for every forbidden pattern?
M: For a permutation $\tau$ let $\mathrm{Av}_n(\tau)$ be the set of $\tau$-avoiding permutations of $[n]$ and let $C_\tau(n)$ be the least worst-case number of comparisons $a_i\overset{?}{<}a_j$ needed by a decision tree that determines the order of $a_1,\dots,a_n$ when the order pattern of $(a_i)$ is promised to lie in $\mathrm{Av}_n(\tau)$. Fredman's bound gives $\log_2|\mathrm{Av}_n(\tau)|\le C_\tau(n)\le\log_2|\mathrm{Av}_n(\tau)|+2n$. Decide whether $C_\tau(n)=\log_2|\mathrm{Av}_n(\tau)|+o(n)$ for every $\tau$. In particular, decide this for $\tau=1324$, whose growth rate is unknown.

title: Monotile assembly threshold
W: With one tile shape, deciding whether a region can be tiled is easy in some cases; with many shapes it is hard. Find the smallest number of shapes where it becomes hard.
M: Find the least $t$ such that some fixed set of $t$ polygons makes "does this finite region admit an exact tiling?" NP-complete, and prove all sets of fewer polygons give polynomial-time problems.

title: The Mandelbrot set at Gaussian rationals
W: Is there an algorithm that takes a complex number with rational real and imaginary parts and decides whether it lies in the Mandelbrot set? Escaping points can be confirmed and attracting cycles can be found. But some Gaussian rationals, such as c = (37 + 16i)/100, lie on the boundary with an irrationally rotating fixed point, and other kinds of boundary point might hide there too.
M: Let $M=\{c\in\mathbb C:\ (f_c^{n}(0))_{n\ge0}\text{ bounded}\}$, $f_c(z)=z^2+c$. Prove or disprove that $M\cap\mathbb Q(i)$ is a decidable subset of $\mathbb Q(i)$. (The parameter $c=\mu/2-\mu^2/4$ with $\mu=(3+4i)/5$ equals $(37+16i)/100\in\partial M$; its fixed point has multiplier $\mu$, which is not a root of unity. Every element of $\mathbb Q(i)\setminus\mathbb Z[i]$ is neither a centre nor a Misiurewicz parameter, since those are algebraic integers.)

title: Chaos in the double pendulum at every energy
W: The planar double pendulum with equal masses and arms is chaotic at moderate energies. Prove it is chaotic at every energy above the rest state, however small.
M: Let $H$ be the Hamiltonian of the planar double pendulum with $m_1=m_2=\ell_1=\ell_2=g=1$, with minimum $E_0$. Prove that for every $E>E_0$ the flow on $\{H=E\}$ has positive topological entropy.

title: Chaos in the symmetric ABC flow
W: The ABC flow with all three coefficients equal to 1 is a classical steady solution of the Euler equations on the 3-torus. Prove it is genuinely chaotic.
M: Prove that the flow of $\dot x=\sin z+\cos y,\ \dot y=\sin x+\cos z,\ \dot z=\sin y+\cos x$ on $\mathbb T^3$ has positive topological entropy.

title: Chaotic billiards in a superellipse
W: The billiard table x⁴+y⁴ ≤ 1 is smooth and convex but has four flat points, so it has no caustics. Show a positive fraction of its phase space is chaotic.
M: Let $\Phi$ be the billiard map of $\{x^4+y^4\le1\}$ with its invariant Liouville measure $\nu$. Prove that the metric entropy $h_\nu(\Phi)$ is positive.

title: Ergodicity of the regular tetrahedron billiard
W: The regular tetrahedron does not tile space, so its billiard cannot be unfolded into a straight-line flow on a torus. Is a billiard ball in it ergodic?
M: Prove or disprove that the billiard flow in a regular tetrahedron in $\mathbb R^3$ is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure on the unit tangent bundle.

title: Four vortices on a square torus
W: Three point vortices on a flat torus are integrable. Show four identical ones are not.
M: Let $H=-\sum_{i<j}G(z_i-z_j)$, with $G$ the Green function of $\mathbb C/(\mathbb Z+i\mathbb Z)$, for four unit vortices. Prove that after reduction by the translation symmetry the system has no real-analytic first integral independent of $H$.

title: Frozen vortices for Kuramoto on a cube
W: Identical Kuramoto oscillators on the grid of a cube surface tend to synchronize. Show that for large grids a stable state that is not synchronized also exists.
M: Let $Q_n$ be the vertex–edge graph of the $n\times n$ subdivided cube surface and $\dot\theta_i=\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i)$. Prove that for all large $n$ there is a linearly stable equilibrium that is not of the form $\theta_i\equiv c$.

title: Integrability of the egg-crate torus
W: Take the surface z = ε sin x sin y over a flat square torus. Show its geodesic flow is never integrable, however small the bumps are.
M: For $\varepsilon>0$ let $g_\varepsilon$ be the metric on $\mathbb R^2/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^2$ induced by the graph $z=\varepsilon\sin x\sin y$ in $\mathbb R^3$. Prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$ the geodesic flow of $g_\varepsilon$ has no real-analytic first integral on $T^*\mathbb T^2\setminus 0$ that is functionally independent of the Hamiltonian.

title: Outer billiards around a superellipse
W: Outer billiards around a smooth convex shape with positive curvature has only bounded orbits. Decide whether this survives for x⁴+y⁴ ≤ 1, whose curvature vanishes at four points.
M: Let $K=\{x^4+y^4\le1\}$ and let $T:\mathbb R^2\setminus K\to\mathbb R^2\setminus K$ be the outer billiard map ($T(p)$ is the reflection of $p$ in the point where the right-hand tangent line from $p$ touches $\partial K$). Decide whether every $T$-orbit is bounded.

title: Two vortices on a cube
W: Two identical point vortices on the surface of a cube have no symmetry to make them integrable. Show their motion is chaotic.
M: Let $G$ be the Green function of the flat unit-cube surface $S$ and $R$ its Robin function. Show the Hamiltonian $H(z_1,z_2)=G(z_1,z_2)+\tfrac12(R(z_1)+R(z_2))$ on $S\times S\setminus\Delta$, with symplectic form $dA_1+dA_2$, has an energy level on which the flow has positive topological entropy.

title: A four-dimensional einstein
W: Find one 4D shape that fills 4D space but only without repeating.
M: Find a connected tile $T\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ that tiles $\mathbb{R}^4$ by isometries but admits no periodic tiling.

title: Capacities of the 4D superball
W: Viterbo's conjecture that all symplectic capacities agree on convex bodies is false in general. Do they agree on the 4D ball x⁴+y⁴+z⁴+w⁴ ≤ 1?
M: Let $U=\{x_1^4+y_1^4+x_2^4+y_2^4\le1\}\subset(\mathbb R^4,\omega_0)$. Decide whether the Gromov width of $U$ equals its Ekeland–Hofer–Zehnder capacity (the minimal action of a closed characteristic on $\partial U$).

title: Cross-polytopes in 4D
W: Every 4D convex body should have the corners of a regular cross-polytope on its boundary.
M: Prove every convex body in $\mathbb{R}^4$ has an inscribed regular cross-polytope.

title: Free-boundary disks in a superball
W: In a round ball the only free-boundary minimal disks are flat. In the superball x⁴+y⁴+z⁴ ≤ 1, is there one that is not a flat slice?
M: Let $B=\{x^4+y^4+z^4\le1\}$. Decide whether there is an embedded minimal disk $\Sigma\subset B$ with $\partial\Sigma\subset\partial B$ meeting $\partial B$ orthogonally that is not contained in a plane.

title: Geodesic squares on surfaces
W: Every smooth closed curve on a convex surface should pass through the corners of a square made of shortest paths.
M: Prove every smooth simple closed curve on a smooth convex surface inscribes a geodesic quadrilateral with equal sides and equal diagonals.

title: Hexagonal Lebesgue covering
W: Find the smallest convex shape that can cover every set of diameter 1, if covering is by translation only, not rotation.
M: Determine $\min\{\mathrm{area}(K):K$ convex, every set of diameter $1$ has a translate inside $K\}$, and prove the minimiser is unique.

title: How nearly can tetrahedra close up
W: A chain of regular tetrahedra glued face to face can never close exactly. Find the exact exponential rate at which the best near-closure improves with chain length.
M: For a regular tetrahedron $T_0$, a chain of length $n$ is $T_0,\dots,T_n$ with $T_{k+1}$ the reflection of $T_k$ in a face not shared with $T_{k-1}$. Let $g(n)$ be the minimum over chains of the Hausdorff distance between $T_n$ and $T_0$ (always positive). Prove that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log g(n)=-\frac{\log 3}{6}$.

title: Icosahedral monotile
W: Find a single 3D tile that fills space and forces five-fold, icosahedral symmetry in every tiling.
M: Find $T\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ tiling space such that every tiling by $T$ has icosahedral symmetry in its hull, or prove none exists.

title: Rotation-proof lattice-point-poor shapes
W: Find the shape in the plane with given area that contains the fewest integer lattice points after any rotation, asymptotically.
M: Determine the convex $K$ of area $A$ minimising $\sup_{\theta}\#(\rho_\theta K\cap\mathbb{Z}^2)$, asymptotically as $A\to\infty$, to second-order term.

title: Rupert superballs
W: The cube can pass through a hole drilled in a copy of itself; the round ball cannot. Show every superball between them, |x|^p+|y|^p+|z|^p ≤ 1 with p > 2, can.
M: Let $B_p=\{|x|^p+|y|^p+|z|^p\le1\}$. Prove that for every $p\in(2,\infty)$ there are orthogonal projections $\pi_1,\pi_2$ onto planes and a rigid motion $\rho$ of the plane with $\rho(\pi_1(B_p))\subset\operatorname{int}\pi_2(B_p)$.

title: Simple closed geodesics on the Fermat quartic
W: On the surface x⁴+y⁴+z⁴ = 1 the nine symmetry planes cut out nine simple closed geodesics. Are there only finitely many simple closed geodesics altogether?
M: Let $S=\{x^4+y^4+z^4=1\}$ with the metric induced from $\mathbb R^3$. The planes $x=0,y=0,z=0,x=\pm y,y=\pm z,x=\pm z$ meet $S$ in simple closed geodesics. Decide whether $S$ has finitely many simple closed geodesics (as unparametrized curves), and if so whether these nine are all of them.

title: Sofa stability
W: Show that any sofa nearly as big as Gerver's must look nearly like Gerver's.
M: Prove a quantitative stability bound: $A(S)\ge A_G-\varepsilon$ implies $d_H(S,G)\le C\varepsilon^{\alpha}$ up to rigid motion.

title: Unit distances in three dimensions after 2026
W: The 2026 number-field idea beat Erdős in the plane. Adapt it to unit distances among points on a sphere in 3D.
M: Prove there are $n$-point sets on the unit sphere $S^2$ with $\ge n^{1+c}$ pairs at distance $1$, for some $c>0$ and infinitely many $n$.

title: Colouring Cayley graphs of the plane lattice
W: Join two points of the integer grid when their difference lies in a fixed finite set D. Given D and a number of colours k, can a computer decide whether this graph can be properly coloured? On the line, periodic colourings settle it. In the plane, the colourings form a tiling-type system that might have no periodic member.
M: For finite symmetric $D\subset\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{0\}$ let $G_D=\mathrm{Cay}(\mathbb Z^2,D)$. Is $\{(D,k): \chi(G_D)\le k\}$ decidable? Equivalently, does every $k$-colourable $G_D$ admit a $k$-colouring periodic under a finite-index subgroup of $\mathbb Z^2$ (which would give decidability, since non-colourability is witnessed by a finite box)? Settle either question.

title: Deciding limit cycles
W: Given a polynomial vector field in the plane with rational coefficients, is there an algorithm that decides whether it has a limit cycle, an isolated closed orbit? Hilbert's 16th problem asks how many limit cycles there can be. This asks only whether their existence is decidable at all.
M: Is the set $\{(P,Q)\in\mathbb Q[x,y]^2:\ \dot x=P,\ \dot y=Q\text{ has a limit cycle}\}$ decidable? Is the set of $(P,Q)$ having at least one non-constant periodic orbit decidable?

title: Formal verification depth of RH
W: The Riemann hypothesis now has a Lean proof. Show it cannot be proved in a weak arithmetic like I-Sigma-1 plus exponentiation, or show it can.
M: Decide whether RH (as a $\Pi^0_1$ sentence) is provable in $\mathrm{I}\Sigma_1$, or in $\mathrm{EFA}$.

title: Logic of random Latin squares
W: Pick a Latin square of order n uniformly at random and view it as a multiplication table on n symbols. Does every first-order statement about it have a limiting probability as n grows? A full zero-one law should fail. For example, the chance that some x satisfies x·x = x presumably tends to 1 − 1/e.
M: Let $L_n$ be a uniformly random Latin square on $[n]$, viewed as the structure $([n],\circ)$ with $x\circ y=L_n(x,y)$. Prove or disprove the first-order convergence law: for every first-order sentence $\varphi$ in the language $\{\circ\}$, $\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr[L_n\models\varphi]$ exists. As a first step, prove that $\Pr[\exists x\ (x\circ x=x)]\to1-e^{-1}$.

title: Proof complexity of the sensitivity theorem
W: Huang proved that any set of more than half the corners of the n-cube contains a corner with at least √n neighbours inside the set. Write this as a propositional formula with one variable per corner. Do polynomial-size proofs exist in resolution, cutting planes or sum-of-squares, measured against the 2^n variables?
M: Let $N=2^n$, $d=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil-1$, and let $\mathrm{SENS}_n$ be the unsatisfiable CNF on variables $x_v$ ($v\in\{0,1\}^n$) plus auxiliary counter variables expressing $\sum_v x_v\ge 2^{n-1}+1$ (sequential-counter encoding), together with, for every $v$ and every $(d+1)$-set $U$ of neighbours of $v$, the clause $\neg x_v\vee\bigvee_{u\in U}\neg x_u$. Does $\mathrm{SENS}_n$ have refutations of size $N^{O(1)}$ in (a) resolution, (b) cutting planes, (c) sum-of-squares (or degree $O(\log N)$ sum-of-squares)? A lower bound of $2^{N^{\Omega(1)}}$ for any of these would also be of interest.

title: Rational rotation numbers of piecewise-linear circle maps
W: A circle homeomorphism built from finitely many straight pieces, with rational break points and rational slopes, has a rotation number. Can a computer decide whether that number is rational? Rational rotation numbers come with periodic orbits through rational points, so they can be detected by search. No method is known to certify irrationality.
M: Let $f:\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ be an orientation-preserving piecewise-linear homeomorphism given by finitely many rational break points and rational slopes (and rational $f(0)$). Is $\{f:\rho(f)\in\mathbb Q\}$ decidable? (If $\rho(f)=p/q$ then $f$ has a periodic orbit, and periodic points solve rational linear equations, so this set is computably enumerable.)

title: Largest prime factor of Markov numbers
W: Show the largest prime factor of Markov numbers tends to infinity.
M: Prove $P(m)\to\infty$ as $m$ runs through Markov numbers.

title: Lonely runner gap for the first n primes
W: For the first n primes as speeds, find the actual loneliness gap asymptotically.
M: Determine the asymptotics of $\delta_n=\sup_t\min_{i\le n}\|tp_i\|$ as $n\to\infty$.

title: Prime Markov triples
W: Show only finitely many Markov triples consist of three primes, or infinitely many.
M: Decide whether infinitely many solutions of $x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz$ have $x,y,z$ all prime.

title: Burgers with degenerate critical dissipation
W: Critical half-Laplacian dissipation keeps Burgers smooth. Let that dissipation switch off at one point of the circle. Do shocks form there?
M: Let $a(x)=1-\cos x$ and consider $u_t+uu_x+\Lambda^{1/2}\big(a\,\Lambda^{1/2}u\big)=0$ on $\mathbb T$, $\Lambda=(-\partial_x^2)^{1/2}$. Decide whether every $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T)$ yields a global smooth solution.

title: Critical NLS mass on the cube
W: Focusing cubic Schrödinger blow-up in 2D needs the ground-state mass. On a cube surface the corners should lower the threshold to three quarters of it.
M: On the flat unit-cube surface $S$, consider $iu_t+\Delta u+|u|^2u=0$. Prove: $H^1$ data with $\|u_0\|_2^2<\tfrac34\|Q\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)}^2$ give global solutions, and for every $m>\tfrac34\|Q\|_2^2$ there is $H^1$ data of mass $m$ blowing up in finite time.

title: Euler with reversed stretching
W: Flip the sign of the vortex-stretching term in the 3D Euler equations, keeping the usual Biot–Savart law. Do smooth solutions stay smooth forever?
M:
Consider $\omega_t+(u\cdot
abla)\omega=-S\omega$ on $\mathbb T^3$, where $u=
abla	imes(-\Delta)^{-1}\omega$ and $S=	frac12(
abla u+
abla u^{T})$. Decide whether every $\omega_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3)$ with mean zero yields a global smooth solution.

title: Heat with a cosine reaction
W: In u_t = u_xx + cos(x)u², the reaction averages to zero, but a second-order effect looks like +u³, the borderline Fujita case. Does every positive start blow up?
M: Prove or disprove: for every $0\le u_0\in C_c(\mathbb R)$, $u_0\not\equiv0$, the solution of $u_t=u_{xx}+\cos(x)\,u^2$ on $\mathbb R$ blows up in finite time.

title: KdV with a cosine coefficient
W: Put a cos x in front of the cubic term of modified KdV on the circle. Energy survives but the L² norm no longer does. Can solutions blow up?
M: Consider $u_t+u_{xxx}+(\cos(x)\,u^3)_x=0$ on $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$, which conserves $\int u$ and $\int(\tfrac12u_x^2-\tfrac14\cos(x)u^4)$ but not $\int u^2$. Decide whether every $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T)$ yields a global smooth solution.

title: Lane–Emden with a shift
W: Replace u² in the five-dimensional Lane–Emden equation by the square of u at a shifted point. Are there still no positive solutions?
M: Let $e\in\mathbb R^5$, $e\ne0$. Decide whether there is a positive $u\in C^2(\mathbb R^5)$ with $-\Delta u(x)=u(x+e)^2$ for all $x$.

title: L⁴ Strichartz on a cube
W: On a flat square torus the L⁴ Strichartz estimate holds with only ε loss of derivatives. Prove the same on the surface of a cube, where corners diffract waves.
M: Let $S$ be the flat unit-cube surface. Prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$, $\|e^{it\Delta}f\|_{L^4([0,1]\times S)}\le C_\varepsilon\|f\|_{H^\varepsilon(S)}$.

title: Minimal-mass blow-up with reflection
W: In the 2D Schrödinger equation where each point feels the density at its mirror point, blow-up needs at least the ground-state mass. Classify the solutions that blow up with exactly that mass.
M: For $i u_t+\Delta u+|u(-x,t)|^2u=0$ on $\mathbb R^2$ with $\|u_0\|_{L^2}=\|Q\|_{L^2}$ ($Q$ the cubic ground state), prove that every $H^1$ solution blowing up in finite time equals, up to phase and scaling, the pseudo-conformal transform of $Q$ centred at the origin.

title: Permanent–Ampère equation
W: Monge–Ampère sets the Hessian determinant to 1, and Jörgens showed its entire convex solutions are quadratics. Swap the determinant for the permanent.
M: Let $u\in C^4(\mathbb R^2)$ satisfy $u_{xx}u_{yy}+u_{xy}^2=1$, $u_{xx}>0$, $2u_{xy}^2<1$ everywhere (ellipticity). Prove or disprove that $u$ is a quadratic polynomial.

title: Quintic Szegő growth
W: The cubic Szegő equation on the circle is integrable and its solutions' high Sobolev norms can grow without bound. Decide what the quintic version does.
M: For $iu_t=\Pi(|u|^4u)$ on $L^2_+(\mathbb T)$ ($\Pi$ the Szegő projector), decide whether there is $u_0\in C^\infty\cap L^2_+$ with $\limsup_{t\to\infty}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}=\infty$ for some $s>\tfrac12$.

title: Riesz-transform Schrödinger equation
W: Couple a 2D Schrödinger wave to the Riesz transform of its own density. Mass is conserved but there is no energy. Do smooth solutions live forever?
M: Consider $i u_t+\Delta u=u\,R_1(|u|^2)$ on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2$, where $\widehat{R_1 f}(\xi)=-i\frac{\xi_1}{|\xi|}\hat f(\xi)$. Decide whether every $u_0\in H^1(\mathbb R^2)$ gives a global solution in $C(\mathbb R,H^1)$.

title: Scattering on the cube corner
W: Defocusing cubic Schrödinger in the plane scatters for all finite-mass data. Show the same on the surface of an infinite cube corner.
M: Let $\mathcal C$ be the flat cone of angle $3\pi/2$ (boundary of an octant). Prove that every $u_0\in L^2(\mathcal C)$ gives a global solution of $iu_t+\Delta u=|u|^2u$ that scatters in $L^2$ as $t\to\pm\infty$.

title: Shifted Fujita equation
W: In the plane, every positive solution of u_t = Δu + u² blows up. Does this survive when the square is replaced by the product of values one unit to the left and right?
M: Let $e=(1,0)$. Prove or disprove: every solution of $u_t=\Delta u+u(x-e,t)\,u(x+e,t)$ on $\mathbb R^2$ with $0\le u_0\in C_c(\mathbb R^2)$, $u_0\not\equiv0$, blows up in finite time.

title: Strauss exponent for an oscillating source
W: The wave equation with source |u|^p in 3D has small-data global existence exactly above the Strauss exponent 1+√2. Find the threshold when the source is multiplied by cos t.
M: For $u_{tt}-\Delta u=\cos(t)\,|u|^p$ on $\mathbb R^{1+3}$ with data $\varepsilon(f,g)$, $f,g\in C_c^\infty$, determine $p_c$ such that for $p>p_c$ solutions are global for all small $\varepsilon$, and for $1<p<p_c$ some data blow up for all small $\varepsilon$; decide whether $p_c=1+\sqrt2$.

title: Unforced blow-up near the forced one
W: Show the known forced Navier–Stokes blow-up can be made to work with forcing that decays to zero at the blow-up time.
M: Prove there exist smooth $u_0$ and $f\in L^1_tL^2_x\cap C^\infty$ with $\|f(t)\|_{L^2}\to0$ as $t\to T^-$ such that the forced 3D NS solution blows up at $T$.

title: Hat Ising universality
W: Magnets on a hat tiling should behave at their critical point exactly like magnets on a square grid.
M: Prove the hat-graph Ising model has critical exponents $\beta=1/8$, $\gamma=7/4$, $\nu=1$.

title: Ising spin at a cube corner
W: Glue three quarter-planes of the square grid into the surface of an infinite cube corner and run the critical Ising model. Prove the corner spin decorrelates with the exponent 7/24 that conformal field theory predicts.
M: Let $\Gamma$ be the union of the three quadrant grids $\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2$ on the faces of the octant boundary, glued along the axes, with apex $o$. For the critical nearest-neighbour Ising model on $\Gamma$ prove $\langle\sigma_o\sigma_x\rangle\asymp|x|^{-7/24}$ as $|x|\to\infty$.

title: Random Wang tiles
W: Pick n random tile types with colored edges. How likely are they to tile the plane?
M: For $n$ Wang tiles with edge colours i.i.d. uniform in $[c]$, find the asymptotics of $\Pr(\text{tiles }\mathbb{Z}^2)$ as $n\to\infty$.

title: Infinite knots in the ABC flow
W: Steady Euler flows can carry knotted streamlines. Show the symmetric ABC flow has closed streamlines tied in infinitely many different knots.
M: Prove that the flow of $\dot x=\sin z+\cos y,\ \dot y=\sin x+\cos z,\ \dot z=\sin y+\cos x$ on $\mathbb T^3$ has null-homotopic periodic orbits lying in embedded balls and realizing infinitely many distinct knot types.

title: Knotted billiards in a regular tetrahedron
W: A billiard ball bouncing periodically inside a regular tetrahedron traces a closed polygon. Show that infinitely many different knot types arise this way.
M: Call a periodic billiard trajectory in a regular tetrahedron $T\subset\mathbb R^3$ admissible if it avoids edges and vertices and is an embedded closed polygon. Prove that the set of knot types of admissible periodic trajectories is infinite.

title: Period-doubling torus bundles
W: Build a once-punctured torus bundle by reading the period-doubling word as a product of the two basic shear matrices. Show its hyperbolic volume per letter settles to a limit as the word grows.
M: Let $W_n\in\{a,b\}^{2^n}$ be the length-$2^n$ prefix of the fixed point of $a\mapsto ab,\ b\mapsto aa$, let $\phi_n$ be $W_n$ with $a\mapsto R=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $b\mapsto L=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$, and let $M_n$ be the (hyperbolic) once-punctured torus bundle with monodromy $\phi_n$. Prove that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathrm{vol}(M_n)/2^n$ exists.

title: Thue–Morse Lorenz knots
W: Turn the first 2^n letters of the Thue–Morse word into a periodic orbit of the Lorenz template. Show these knots are eventually hyperbolic and their volume grows proportionally to the word length.
M: Let $K_n$ be the Lorenz knot whose Lorenz word is the length-$2^n$ Thue–Morse prefix $t_0\cdots t_{2^n-1}$ with $0\mapsto x$, $1\mapsto y$ (this word is primitive). Prove that $S^3\setminus K_n$ is hyperbolic for all sufficiently large $n$ and that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathrm{vol}(S^3\setminus K_n)/2^n$ exists and is positive.
